chapters.title: Nehemiah's Prayer
chapters.html:
Nehemiah 1

News from Jerusalem

1The words of Nehemiah son of Hacaliah.

And it came to pass in the month of Chislev, in the twentieth year, as I was in Susa the citadel,

2that Hanani, one of my brothers, came with some men from Judah. I asked them about the Jews who had escaped, those who were left from the captivity, and about Jerusalem.

3They said to me, "The remnant there in the province who are left from the captivity are in great trouble and disgrace. The wall of Jerusalem is broken down, and its gates have been burned with fire."

4When I heard these words, I sat down and wept and mourned for days, and I was fasting and praying before the God of heaven.

The Prayer

5I said, "Please, LORD, God of heaven, the great and awesome God, who keeps covenant and loyal love with those who love Him and keep His commandments,

6let Your ear be attentive and Your eyes open, to hear the prayer of Your servant that I am praying before You today, day and night, for the sons of Israel Your servants, confessing the sins of the sons of Israel, which we have sinned against You. Both I and my father's house have sinned.

7We have acted very corruptly against You and have not kept the commandments, the statutes and the rules that You commanded Moses Your servant.

8Remember the word that You commanded Moses Your servant, saying, 'If you break faith, I will scatter you among the peoples;

9but if you return to Me and keep My commandments and do them, even if your outcasts are at the end of the heavens, I will gather them from there and bring them to the place that I have chosen to make My name dwell there.'

10They are Your servants and Your people, whom You redeemed by Your great power and by Your strong hand.

11Please, Lord, let Your ear be attentive to the prayer of Your servant and to the prayer of Your servants who delight to fear Your name. Give success to Your servant today, and grant him mercy before this man."

I was cupbearer to the king.

Notes

  • v1 "The words of Nehemiah son of Hacaliah" — the book opens as a man's own account, and most of it is told in the first person.

  • v1 "in the month of Chislev, in the twentieth year" — the twentieth year of Artaxerxes (2:1), the ninth month of the year; the request to the king comes four months later, in Nisan.

  • v5 "the great and awesome God, who keeps covenant and loyal love with those who love Him" — the words of Moses: the faithful God, who keeps covenant and loyal love with those who love Him and keep His commandments (Deuteronomy 7:9). Daniel's prayer opens with the same words (Daniel 9:4).

  • v6 "let Your ear be attentive and Your eyes open" — Solomon's prayer at the dedication of the house: let Your eyes be open and Your ears attentive to the prayer made in this place (2 Chronicles 6:40). Both I and my father's house have sinned: he confesses with the people, not about them.

  • vv8–9 "If you break faith, I will scatter you… even if your outcasts are at the end of the heavens, I will gather them from there" — not one verse but the sense of several: I will scatter you among the nations (Leviticus 26:33), and if your outcasts are at the end of the heavens, from there the LORD your God will gather you (Deuteronomy 30:4). Break faith is ma'al, Ezra's word for the sin (Ezra 9:2).

  • v10 "by Your great power and by Your strong hand" — Moses' plea after the golden calf: whom You brought out of the land of Egypt with great power and with a strong hand (Exodus 32:11).

  • v11 "before this man… I was cupbearer to the king" — mashqeh, the office of Pharaoh's chief cupbearer in Joseph's story (Genesis 40:1–2). In the prayer, the king of Persia is this man.

chapters.title: Nehemiah Sent to Jerusalem
chapters.html:
Nehemiah 2

Before the King

1And it came to pass in the month of Nisan, in the twentieth year of Artaxerxes the king, when wine was before him, that I took up the wine and gave it to the king. I had not been sad in his presence before.

2The king said to me, "Why is your face sad, though you are not sick? This is nothing but sadness of heart." I was very much afraid.

3I said to the king, "May the king live forever! Why should my face not be sad, when the city, the place of my fathers' graves, lies in ruins, and its gates have been consumed by fire?"

4The king said to me, "What are you asking for?" So I prayed to the God of heaven,

5and I said to the king, "If it pleases the king, and if your servant has found favor in your sight, send me to Judah, to the city of my fathers' graves, that I may rebuild it."

6The king said to me, with the queen sitting beside him, "How long will your journey be, and when will you return?" So it pleased the king to send me, and I set him a time.

7I said to the king, "If it pleases the king, let letters be given me to the governors of the province Beyond the River, so that they will let me pass through until I come to Judah,

8and a letter to Asaph, the keeper of the king's forest, that he may give me timber to make beams for the gates of the citadel of the house, for the wall of the city and for the house that I will occupy." The king granted me this, for the good hand of my God was on me.

9I came to the governors of the province Beyond the River and gave them the king's letters. The king had sent with me officers of the army and horsemen.

10When Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the Ammonite servant heard this, it displeased them greatly that someone had come to seek the good of the sons of Israel.

The Walls Inspected by Night

11I came to Jerusalem and was there three days.

12Then I arose in the night, I and a few men with me. I told no one what my God had put into my heart to do for Jerusalem. There was no animal with me except the animal I was riding.

13I went out by night through the Valley Gate toward the Dragon's Spring and to the Dung Gate, and I examined the walls of Jerusalem, which were broken down, and its gates, which had been consumed by fire.

14Then I went on to the Fountain Gate and to the King's Pool, but there was no room for the animal under me to pass.

15So I went up by the valley in the night and examined the wall. Then I turned back and entered by the Valley Gate, and so returned.

16The officials did not know where I had gone or what I was doing, for I had not yet told the Jews, the priests, the nobles, the officials or the rest who were to do the work.

"Let Us Rise and Build"

17Then I said to them, "You see the trouble we are in, how Jerusalem lies in ruins and its gates are burned with fire. Come, let us build the wall of Jerusalem, so that we may no longer be a disgrace."

18I told them of the hand of my God, which had been good on me, and also of the words the king had spoken to me. They said, "Let us rise and build." So they strengthened their hands for the good work.

19But when Sanballat the Horonite, Tobiah the Ammonite servant and Geshem the Arab heard of it, they mocked us and despised us and said, "What is this thing you are doing? Are you rebelling against the king?"

20I answered them, "The God of heaven, He will give us success, and we His servants will rise and build. But you have no portion, no right and no memorial in Jerusalem."

Notes

  • vv1–2 "I had not been sad in his presence… Why is your face sad, though you are not sick?" — maddua panekha ra'im, the question Joseph put to Pharaoh's cupbearer in prison: Why are your faces bad today? (Genesis 40:7). Now the cupbearer is the one with the sad face, and the king asks.

  • v3 "the city, the place of my fathers' graves" — he does not name Jerusalem. A letter to an Artaxerxes had called it that rebellious and wicked city, and the king had stopped its rebuilding (Ezra 4:12, 21); Nehemiah speaks of his fathers' graves.

  • v4 "So I prayed to the God of heaven, and I said to the king" — the prayer comes between the king's question and the answer, in the time it takes to draw breath.

  • v6 "with the queen sitting beside him" — ha-shegal, the word of the psalm, the queen stands at your right hand in gold of Ophir (Psalm 45:9).

  • v8 "the keeper of the king's forest" — pardes, a Persian word for an enclosed park, the word behind English paradise.

  • v8 "for the good hand of my God was on me" — Ezra's refrain (Ezra 7:6, 9, 28; 8:18, 22, 31), now in Nehemiah's mouth (also v18).

  • v10 "Tobiah the Ammonite servant" — the law says No Ammonite… shall enter the assembly of the LORD (Deuteronomy 23:3), and the book will end with Tobiah turned out of a chamber of the house (13:1–8).

  • v18 "So they strengthened their hands" — va-yechazzequ yedeihem, the reverse of the people of the land who kept weakening the hands of the people of Judah (Ezra 4:4).

  • v20 "no portion, no right and no memorial in Jerusalem" — cheleq u-tsedaqah ve-zikkaron: no share of the land, no legal claim, and no name remembered there.

chapters.title: The Builders of the Wall
chapters.html:
Nehemiah 3

From the Sheep Gate to the Valley Gate

1Then Eliashib the high priest rose up with his brothers the priests, and they built the Sheep Gate. They consecrated it and set up its doors. They consecrated it as far as the Tower of the Hundred, as far as the Tower of Hananel.

2Next to him the men of Jericho built, and next to them Zaccur son of Imri built.

3The sons of Hassenaah built the Fish Gate. They laid its beams and set up its doors, its bolts and its bars.

4Next to them Meremoth son of Uriah, son of Hakkoz, repaired. Next to them Meshullam son of Berechiah, son of Meshezabel, repaired. Next to them Zadok son of Baana repaired.

5Next to them the Tekoites repaired, but their nobles would not put their necks to the work of their lord.

6Joiada son of Paseah and Meshullam son of Besodeiah repaired the Old Gate. They laid its beams and set up its doors, its bolts and its bars.

7Next to them Melatiah the Gibeonite and Jadon the Meronothite, the men of Gibeon and of Mizpah, repaired, for the seat of the governor of the province Beyond the River.

8Next to him Uzziel son of Harhaiah, of the goldsmiths, repaired. Next to him Hananiah, one of the perfumers, repaired, and they restored Jerusalem as far as the Broad Wall.

9Next to them Rephaiah son of Hur, ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, repaired.

10Next to them Jedaiah son of Harumaph repaired opposite his own house, and next to him Hattush son of Hashabneiah repaired.

11Malchijah son of Harim and Hasshub son of Pahath-moab repaired another section and the Tower of the Ovens.

12Next to him Shallum son of Hallohesh, ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, repaired, he and his daughters.

13Hanun and the inhabitants of Zanoah repaired the Valley Gate. They built it and set up its doors, its bolts and its bars, and repaired a thousand cubits of the wall, as far as the Dung Gate.

From the Dung Gate to the Water Gate

14Malchijah son of Rechab, ruler of the district of Beth-haccherem, repaired the Dung Gate. He built it and set up its doors, its bolts and its bars.

15Shallun son of Col-hozeh, ruler of the district of Mizpah, repaired the Fountain Gate. He built it, roofed it and set up its doors, its bolts and its bars. He also repaired the wall of the Pool of Shelah by the king's garden, as far as the steps that go down from the City of David.

16After him Nehemiah son of Azbuk, ruler of half the district of Beth-zur, repaired as far as a point opposite the tombs of David, as far as the pool that had been made, and as far as the house of the mighty men.

17After him the Levites repaired: Rehum son of Bani. Next to him Hashabiah, ruler of half the district of Keilah, repaired for his district.

18After him their brothers repaired: Bavvai son of Henadad, ruler of half the district of Keilah.

19Next to him Ezer son of Jeshua, ruler of Mizpah, repaired another section, opposite the ascent to the armory at the angle.

20After him Baruch son of Zaccai zealously repaired another section, from the angle to the door of the house of Eliashib the high priest.

21After him Meremoth son of Uriah, son of Hakkoz, repaired another section, from the door of the house of Eliashib to the end of the house of Eliashib.

22After him the priests, the men of the surrounding plain, repaired.

23After them Benjamin and Hasshub repaired opposite their own house. After them Azariah son of Maaseiah, son of Ananiah, repaired beside his own house.

24After him Binnui son of Henadad repaired another section, from the house of Azariah to the angle and to the corner.

25Palal son of Uzai repaired opposite the angle and the tower that projects from the upper house of the king at the court of the guard. After him Pedaiah son of Parosh

26and the temple servants who lived on the Ophel repaired as far as a point opposite the Water Gate on the east and the projecting tower.

From the Ophel Back to the Sheep Gate

27After them the Tekoites repaired another section, opposite the great projecting tower as far as the wall of the Ophel.

28Above the Horse Gate the priests repaired, each opposite his own house.

29After them Zadok son of Immer repaired opposite his own house. After him Shemaiah son of Shecaniah, the keeper of the East Gate, repaired.

30After him Hananiah son of Shelemiah and Hanun the sixth son of Zalaph repaired another section. After him Meshullam son of Berechiah repaired opposite his own chamber.

31After him Malchijah, one of the goldsmiths, repaired as far as the house of the temple servants and of the merchants, opposite the Muster Gate, and as far as the upper room of the corner.

32Between the upper room of the corner and the Sheep Gate the goldsmiths and the merchants repaired.

Notes

  • vv1, 32 "the Sheep Gate" — the list begins and ends at the same gate and goes once around the city, gate by gate, section by section.

  • vv4–32 "repaired" — hecheziq, made strong, the verb of the chapter, said again and again of every family and every section. Next to him… after him carries the list around the wall as the work was done, side by side.

  • v1 "Eliashib the high priest… consecrated it" — the high priest's family takes the first gate, near the house, and consecrates it. His own house is on the wall (vv20–21).

  • v5 "their nobles would not put their necks to the work of their lord" — tsavvaram, their neck, as an ox's neck under a yoke. Adoneihem, their lords, may be Nehemiah and the officials, or the Lord. The Tekoites themselves did a second section (v27).

  • v8 "they restored Jerusalem" — va-ya'azvu, a verb that usually means leave, abandon. Here it can only mean something done to the wall; restored is the sense most widely given, and it is uncertain.

  • v12 "he and his daughters" — the only women named in the work on the wall.

  • v15 "the Pool of Shelah" — ha-Shelach, from shalach, to send, the conduit that sends the water; Isaiah's the waters of Shiloah that go gently (Isaiah 8:6) is written with the same letters.

  • v20 "zealously" — hecherah, from charah, the verb of anger that burns; here it is said of the work.

chapters.title: Building with a Weapon in Hand
chapters.html:
Nehemiah 4

The Mockery of Sanballat and Tobiah

1And it came to pass, when Sanballat heard that we were building the wall, that he was angry and greatly enraged, and he mocked the Jews.

2He said before his brothers and the army of Samaria, "What are these feeble Jews doing? Will they restore it for themselves? Will they sacrifice? Will they finish in a day? Will they bring the stones back to life out of the heaps of rubble, burned as they are?"

3Tobiah the Ammonite was beside him, and he said, "Even what they are building, if a fox went up on it, he would break down their stone wall!"

4Hear, our God, for we are despised. Turn their taunt back on their own heads, and give them up to be plundered in a land of captivity.

5Do not cover their iniquity, and do not let their sin be blotted out from before You, for they have provoked You to anger before the builders.

6So we built the wall, and the whole wall was joined together up to half its height, for the people had a heart to work.

The Plot and the Guard

7When Sanballat and Tobiah, the Arabs, the Ammonites and the Ashdodites heard that the repair of the walls of Jerusalem was going forward and that the breaches were beginning to be closed, they were very angry,

8and they all plotted together to come and fight against Jerusalem and throw it into confusion.

9But we prayed to our God and set a guard against them day and night because of them.

10In Judah they said, "The strength of the burden bearers is failing, and there is too much rubble. We cannot build the wall."

11Our adversaries said, "They will not know or see until we come into their midst and kill them and stop the work."

12When the Jews who lived near them came, they said to us ten times, "From every place where you turn, they will come against us."

13So I stationed the people in the lowest parts of the space behind the wall, in the open places. I stationed the people by families, with their swords, their spears and their bows.

14I looked, and I rose and said to the nobles, the officials and the rest of the people, "Do not be afraid of them. Remember the Lord, great and awesome, and fight for your brothers, your sons, your daughters, your wives and your homes."

15When our enemies heard that it was known to us, and God had frustrated their plan, we all returned to the wall, each to his work.

A Sword at Every Side

16And it came to pass from that day on that half of my servants did the work, while the other half held the spears, the shields, the bows and the armor, and the officers stood behind the whole house of Judah,

17who were building the wall. Those who carried burdens were loaded in such a way that each did the work with one hand and held his weapon with the other.

18Each of the builders had his sword strapped at his side as he built, and the man who sounded the horn was beside me.

19I said to the nobles, the officials and the rest of the people, "The work is great and spread out, and we are separated on the wall, far from one another.

20Wherever you hear the sound of the horn, gather to us there. Our God will fight for us."

21So we did the work, while half of them held the spears, from the break of dawn until the stars came out.

22At that time I also said to the people, "Let every man and his servant spend the night inside Jerusalem, so that they may be a guard for us by night and work by day."

23Neither I nor my brothers nor my servants nor the men of the guard who followed me took off our clothes; each kept his weapon at the water.

Notes

  • vv1–23 — the Hebrew numbers vv1–6 as 3:33–38 and vv7–23 as 4:1–17. The rendering follows the English numbering.

  • v2 "Will they bring the stones back to life" — ha-yechayyu, make live, the verb for raising the dead, used of burned stones in the rubble.

  • vv4–5 "Do not cover their iniquity, and do not let their sin be blotted out from before You" — the words of Jeremiah's prayer against those who plotted his death: Do not atone for their iniquity, and do not blot out their sin from before You (Jeremiah 18:23).

  • v12 "From every place where you turn, they will come against us" — the Hebrew is hard: from all the places that you return to us. The Greek reads They are coming up against us from all the places. The neighbors' warning is clear; its exact words are not.

  • v14 "Remember the Lord, great and awesome" — the words of Nehemiah's first prayer, the great and awesome God (1:5), now a battle cry.

  • v17 "each did the work with one hand and held his weapon with the other" — shelach, a weapon, a thrown spear or dart; the Greek has bolida, a javelin.

  • v20 "Our God will fight for us" — the word of Moses at the sea: The LORD will fight for you (Exodus 14:14).

  • v23 "each kept his weapon at the water" — the Hebrew is four words, ish shilcho ha-mayim, each his weapon, the water, and its sense is uncertain: perhaps that even going for water a man took his weapon. The Greek leaves the words out.

I looked, and I rose and said to the nobles, the officials and the rest of the people, "Do not be afraid of them. Remember the Lord, great and awesome, and fight for your brothers, your sons, your daughters, your wives and your homes."

And it came to pass from that day on that half of my servants did the work, while the other half held the spears, the shields, the bows and the armor, and the officers stood behind the whole house of Judah,
who were building the wall. Those who carried burdens were loaded in such a way that each did the work with one hand and held his weapon with the other.
Each of the builders had his sword strapped at his side as he built, and the man who sounded the horn was beside me.
I said to the nobles, the officials and the rest of the people, "The work is great and spread out, and we are separated on the wall, far from one another.
Wherever you hear the sound of the horn, gather to us there. Our God will fight for us."
So we did the work, while half of them held the spears, from the break of dawn until the stars came out.
At that time I also said to the people, "Let every man and his servant spend the night inside Jerusalem, so that they may be a guard for us by night and work by day."
Neither I nor my brothers nor my servants nor the men of the guard who followed me took off our clothes; each kept his weapon at the water.

chapters.title: The Outcry of the Poor
chapters.html:
Nehemiah 5

The Outcry

1There was a great outcry of the people and their wives against their brothers the Jews.

2Some were saying, "With our sons and our daughters, we are many. Let us get grain, so that we may eat and live."

3Some were saying, "We are mortgaging our fields, our vineyards and our houses to get grain in the famine."

4Some were saying, "We have borrowed money for the king's tax on our fields and our vineyards.

5Our flesh is like the flesh of our brothers, and our children are like their children, yet we are forcing our sons and our daughters into slavery. Some of our daughters have already been forced into it, and it is not in our power to help it, for our fields and our vineyards belong to others."

Nehemiah Rebukes the Nobles

6I was very angry when I heard their outcry and these words.

7I took counsel with myself and brought charges against the nobles and the officials. I said to them, "You are exacting interest, each from his brother!" Then I held a great assembly against them.

8I said to them, "We, as far as we were able, have bought back our brothers the Jews who had been sold to the nations, but you are selling your own brothers, so that they may be sold to us!" They were silent and could find nothing to say.

9I said, "What you are doing is not good. Should you not walk in the fear of our God, because of the taunts of the nations, our enemies?

10I too, and my brothers and my servants, are lending them money and grain. Let us stop this interest.

11Give back to them this very day their fields, their vineyards, their olive groves and their houses, and the hundredth part of the money, the grain, the new wine and the oil that you are exacting from them."

12They said, "We will give it back and require nothing from them. We will do as you say." I called the priests and made them swear to do as they had promised.

13I also shook out the fold of my garment and said, "So may God shake out every man from his house and from his labor who does not keep this promise. So may he be shaken out and emptied." All the assembly said, "Amen," and praised the LORD. The people did as they had promised.

Nehemiah's Example

14Moreover, from the day I was appointed to be their governor in the land of Judah, from the twentieth year to the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes the king, twelve years, neither I nor my brothers ate the governor's food allowance.

15The former governors who were before me laid heavy burdens on the people and took from them food and wine, besides forty shekels of silver. Even their servants lorded it over the people. But I did not do so, because of the fear of God.

16I also held fast to the work on this wall, and we bought no land, and all my servants were gathered there for the work.

17At my table were a hundred and fifty men, Jews and officials, besides those who came to us from the nations around us.

18What was prepared for one day was one ox and six choice sheep, and birds were prepared for me, and every ten days all kinds of wine in abundance. Yet for all this I did not ask for the governor's food allowance, because the service was heavy on this people.

19Remember me, my God, for good, for all that I have done for this people.

Notes

  • vv1, 6 "a great outcry… their outcry" — tsa'aqah, za'aqah, the cry the LORD heard from Israel in Egypt: I have heard their outcry because of their taskmasters (Exodus 3:7). Now the cry is against brothers.

  • v5 "Our flesh is like the flesh of our brothers" — ki-vsar acheinu besarenu. The words Judah used of Joseph when he proposed to sell him: he is our brother, our flesh (Genesis 37:27). The poor use them against brothers who are selling them.

  • v7 "You are exacting interest, each from his brother" — massa… nosh'im, from nasha, to lend at interest, the word of the law: you shall not be a creditor to him (Exodus 22:25); You shall not charge interest to your brother (Deuteronomy 23:19).

  • v8 "We… have bought back our brothers… but you are selling your own brothers" — the law of redemption: a brother sold to a guest living among you may be bought back by his kin (Leviticus 25:47–49), and a brother who sells himself to you must not be made to serve as a slave (25:39).

  • v13 "I also shook out the fold of my garment" — chotsni, the fold at the chest where things were carried. Emptied before them, it shows what will happen to any man who breaks the oath.

  • v14 "from the twentieth year to the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes" — the year Nehemiah came (2:1) to the year he went back to the king (13:6).

  • v19 "Remember me, my God, for good" — Nehemiah's short prayer, his own signature. It returns, in nearly the same words, at the end of the book (13:14, 22, 31).

chapters.title: The Wall Finished
chapters.html:
Nehemiah 6

The Plots against Nehemiah

1And it came to pass, when it was reported to Sanballat and Tobiah and to Geshem the Arab and to the rest of our enemies that I had built the wall and that no breach was left in it, though up to that time I had not set up the doors in the gates,

2that Sanballat and Geshem sent to me, saying, "Come, let us meet together at Kephirim in the plain of Ono." But they were planning to do me harm.

3So I sent messengers to them, saying, "I am doing a great work and cannot come down. Why should the work stop while I leave it and come down to you?"

4They sent to me four times in this way, and I answered them in the same way.

5The fifth time Sanballat sent his servant to me in the same way, with an open letter in his hand.

6In it was written: "It is reported among the nations, and Geshem says it too, that you and the Jews are planning to rebel; that is why you are building the wall. According to these reports, you are to become their king,

7and you have also set up prophets to proclaim about you in Jerusalem, 'There is a king in Judah.' Now this will be reported to the king according to these words. So now come, and let us take counsel together."

8I sent to him, saying, "No such things as you say have been done; you are inventing them out of your own heart."

9For they all wanted to frighten us, thinking, "Their hands will drop from the work, and it will not be done." But now, strengthen my hands.

The Hired Prophet

10I went into the house of Shemaiah son of Delaiah, son of Mehetabel, who was shut in at home, and he said, "Let us meet at the house of God, inside the temple, and let us shut the doors of the temple, for they are coming to kill you. By night they are coming to kill you."

11But I said, "Should a man like me run away? Would a man like me go into the temple and live? I will not go in."

12Then I understood that God had not sent him, but that he had spoken the prophecy against me because Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him.

13He was hired for this purpose, that I should be afraid and act in this way and sin, and so they would have a bad name to taunt me with.

14Remember, my God, Tobiah and Sanballat according to these deeds of theirs, and also Noadiah the prophetess and the rest of the prophets who wanted to make me afraid.

The Wall Finished

15So the wall was finished on the twenty-fifth day of the month of Elul, in fifty-two days.

16When all our enemies heard of it, all the nations around us were afraid and fell greatly in their own eyes, for they knew that this work had been done by our God.

17In those days also the nobles of Judah sent many letters to Tobiah, and Tobiah's letters came to them.

18For many in Judah were bound to him by oath, because he was the son-in-law of Shecaniah son of Arah, and his son Jehohanan had married the daughter of Meshullam son of Berechiah.

19They also kept speaking of his good deeds in my presence and reporting my words to him, and Tobiah sent letters to make me afraid.

Notes

  • v3 "I sent messengers to them, saying, 'I am doing a great work'" — mal'akhim, messengers, and melakhah, work, from the same root, la'akh, to send on an errand. They send for him; his errand is the wall.

  • v5 "an open letter" — not sealed, so that the servant and anyone along the way could read it. The charge of rebellion is spread as it is delivered.

  • v7 "There is a king in Judah" — the charge Ezra's enemies brought: a city rebellious and harmful to kings (Ezra 4:15).

  • vv10–11 "inside the temple… would a man like me go into the temple and live?" — ha-heikhal, the house itself, where only the priests may enter. The law says the outsider who comes near shall be put to death (Numbers 18:7), and King Uzziah was struck with blight for going in (2 Chronicles 26:16–21). Nehemiah is not a priest; to hide there would itself be the sin (v13).

  • v14 "Noadiah the prophetess" — ha-nevi'ah, the title of Miriam, Deborah and Huldah. Here it is given to a prophetess who works against him.

  • v15 "the twenty-fifth day of the month of Elul, in fifty-two days" — Elul is the sixth month. The wall that had lain broken since Babylon burned it was closed in less than two months.

  • v16 "fell greatly in their own eyes" — va-yippelu me'od be-eineihem: their confidence fell, as the wall rose.

  • v18 "the son-in-law of Shecaniah… the daughter of Meshullam son of Berechiah" — Meshullam built two sections of the wall (3:4, 30). Tobiah the Ammonite is married into the families doing the work.

chapters.title: The Record of the First Return
chapters.html:
Nehemiah 7

The City Guarded

1And it came to pass, when the wall had been built and I had set up the doors, that the gatekeepers, the singers and the Levites were appointed.

2I put my brother Hanani, and Hananiah the commander of the citadel, in charge of Jerusalem, for he was a faithful man and feared God more than many.

3I said to them, "The gates of Jerusalem are not to be opened until the sun is hot, and while the guards are still standing there, let them shut the doors and bar them. Appoint guards from the inhabitants of Jerusalem, each at his post and each opposite his own house."

4The city was wide and large, but the people in it were few, and no houses had been built.

The Record Found

5Then my God put it into my heart to gather the nobles, the officials and the people to be enrolled by genealogy. I found the book of the genealogy of those who came up at the first, and I found written in it:

6These are the people of the province who came up out of the captivity of the exiles, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried away. They returned to Jerusalem and Judah, each to his own town.

7They came with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Azariah, Raamiah, Nahamani, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispereth, Bigvai, Nehum and Baanah. The number of the men of the people of Israel:

8the sons of Parosh, two thousand one hundred and seventy-two;

9the sons of Shephatiah, three hundred and seventy-two;

10the sons of Arah, six hundred and fifty-two;

11the sons of Pahath-moab, of the sons of Jeshua and Joab, two thousand eight hundred and eighteen;

12the sons of Elam, one thousand two hundred and fifty-four;

13the sons of Zattu, eight hundred and forty-five;

14the sons of Zaccai, seven hundred and sixty;

15the sons of Binnui, six hundred and forty-eight;

16the sons of Bebai, six hundred and twenty-eight;

17the sons of Azgad, two thousand three hundred and twenty-two;

18the sons of Adonikam, six hundred and sixty-seven;

19the sons of Bigvai, two thousand and sixty-seven;

20the sons of Adin, six hundred and fifty-five;

21the sons of Ater, of Hezekiah, ninety-eight;

22the sons of Hashum, three hundred and twenty-eight;

23the sons of Bezai, three hundred and twenty-four;

24the sons of Hariph, one hundred and twelve;

25the sons of Gibeon, ninety-five;

26the men of Bethlehem and Netophah, one hundred and eighty-eight;

27the men of Anathoth, one hundred and twenty-eight;

28the men of Beth-azmaveth, forty-two;

29the men of Kiriath-jearim, Chephirah and Beeroth, seven hundred and forty-three;

30the men of Ramah and Geba, six hundred and twenty-one;

31the men of Michmas, one hundred and twenty-two;

32the men of Bethel and Ai, one hundred and twenty-three;

33the men of the other Nebo, fifty-two;

34the sons of the other Elam, one thousand two hundred and fifty-four;

35the sons of Harim, three hundred and twenty;

36the sons of Jericho, three hundred and forty-five;

37the sons of Lod, Hadid and Ono, seven hundred and twenty-one;

38the sons of Senaah, three thousand nine hundred and thirty.

39The priests: the sons of Jedaiah, of the house of Jeshua, nine hundred and seventy-three;

40the sons of Immer, one thousand and fifty-two;

41the sons of Pashhur, one thousand two hundred and forty-seven;

42the sons of Harim, one thousand and seventeen.

43The Levites: the sons of Jeshua, of Kadmiel, of the sons of Hodevah, seventy-four.

44The singers: the sons of Asaph, one hundred and forty-eight.

45The gatekeepers: the sons of Shallum, the sons of Ater, the sons of Talmon, the sons of Akkub, the sons of Hatita and the sons of Shobai, one hundred and thirty-eight.

46The temple servants: the sons of Ziha, the sons of Hasupha, the sons of Tabbaoth,

47the sons of Keros, the sons of Sia, the sons of Padon,

48the sons of Lebana, the sons of Hagaba, the sons of Shalmai,

49the sons of Hanan, the sons of Giddel, the sons of Gahar,

50the sons of Reaiah, the sons of Rezin, the sons of Nekoda,

51the sons of Gazzam, the sons of Uzza, the sons of Paseah,

52the sons of Besai, the sons of the Meunim, the sons of the Nephishesim,

53the sons of Bakbuk, the sons of Hakupha, the sons of Harhur,

54the sons of Bazlith, the sons of Mehida, the sons of Harsha,

55the sons of Barkos, the sons of Sisera, the sons of Temah,

56the sons of Neziah and the sons of Hatipha.

57The sons of Solomon's servants: the sons of Sotai, the sons of Sophereth, the sons of Perida,

58the sons of Jaala, the sons of Darkon, the sons of Giddel,

59the sons of Shephatiah, the sons of Hattil, the sons of Pochereth-hazzebaim and the sons of Amon.

60All the temple servants and the sons of Solomon's servants were three hundred and ninety-two.

61These were the ones who came up from Tel-melah, Tel-harsha, Cherub, Addon and Immer, but they could not show their fathers' houses or their descent, whether they were of Israel:

62the sons of Delaiah, the sons of Tobiah and the sons of Nekoda, six hundred and forty-two.

63Of the priests: the sons of Hobaiah, the sons of Hakkoz and the sons of Barzillai, who had taken a wife from the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite and was called by their name.

64These searched for their entry among those enrolled by genealogy, but it was not found, so they were barred from the priesthood as unclean.

65The governor told them that they were not to eat of the most holy things until a priest arose with Urim and Thummim.

66The whole assembly together was forty-two thousand three hundred and sixty,

67besides their male and female servants, who were seven thousand three hundred and thirty-seven; and they had two hundred and forty-five singing men and singing women.

68(This verse is not in the Hebrew or the Greek of Nehemiah; see the note.)

69Their camels were four hundred and thirty-five, and their donkeys six thousand seven hundred and twenty.

Gifts for the Work

70Some of the heads of the fathers' houses gave to the work. The governor gave to the treasury a thousand darics of gold, fifty basins and five hundred and thirty priests' garments.

71Some of the heads of the fathers' houses gave to the treasury of the work twenty thousand darics of gold and two thousand two hundred minas of silver.

72What the rest of the people gave was twenty thousand darics of gold, two thousand minas of silver and sixty-seven priests' garments.

73So the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, some of the people, the temple servants and all Israel lived in their towns.

When the seventh month came, the sons of Israel were in their towns.

Notes

  • vv1–73 — the Hebrew has 72 verses here. English v68 has no counterpart in the Hebrew, and vv69–73 are Hebrew vv68–72. The rendering follows the English numbering.

  • vv6–73 and Ezra 2:1–70 — the same list, copied from the book of the genealogy of those who came up at the first (v5). Many numbers differ, and some names: Ezra's Seraiah, Reelaiah… Rehum are here Azariah, Raamiah… Nehum, and Nehemiah names twelve leaders where Ezra names eleven. The listed numbers here add up to 31,089; Ezra's add up to 29,818; both give the same total, 42,360 (v66; Ezra 2:64).

  • v2 "for he was a faithful man and feared God more than many" — ki-ish emet, a man of truth. Nehemiah's test for the man who holds the gates.

  • v3 "until the sun is hot" — not at dawn: the gates stay shut until the day is well begun and the city is awake to guard them.

  • v4 "the people in it were few, and no houses had been built" — the wall is done, but the city inside it is nearly empty. The list that follows is found to fill it (11:1–2).

  • v68 — English Bibles have a verse here, Their horses were seven hundred and thirty-six, their mules two hundred and forty-five, the same as Ezra 2:66. The Hebrew of Nehemiah lacks it, and so does the Greek, which goes straight from the singers to the camels. The verse number is kept so that the numbering matches, and the line is left out.

  • v73 "When the seventh month came" — the same words that open Ezra 3:1. In Ezra they lead to the rebuilding of the altar; here, to the reading of the book of the instruction (8:1).

Gifts for the Work

chapters.title: Ezra Reads the Instruction
chapters.html:
Nehemiah 8

The Reading at the Water Gate

1All the people gathered as one man into the square before the Water Gate, and they told Ezra the scribe to bring the book of the instruction of Moses, which the LORD had commanded Israel.

2So Ezra the priest brought the instruction before the assembly, men and women and all who could listen with understanding, on the first day of the seventh month.

3He read from it in the square before the Water Gate from daybreak until midday, in the presence of the men and the women and those who could understand, and the ears of all the people were on the book of the instruction.

4Ezra the scribe stood on a wooden platform that they had made for the purpose. Beside him on his right stood Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah and Maaseiah, and on his left Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hashbaddanah, Zechariah and Meshullam.

5Ezra opened the book in the sight of all the people, for he was above all the people, and as he opened it all the people stood up.

6Ezra blessed the LORD, the great God, and all the people answered, "Amen, Amen," lifting up their hands. They bowed down and worshiped the LORD with their faces to the ground.

7Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan and Pelaiah, the Levites, helped the people to understand the instruction, while the people stood in their places.

8They read from the book, from the instruction of God, clearly, and gave the sense, so that the people understood the reading.

"The Joy of the LORD Is Your Strength"

9Nehemiah, who was the governor, and Ezra the priest, the scribe, and the Levites who taught the people said to all the people, "This day is holy to the LORD your God. Do not mourn or weep." For all the people were weeping as they heard the words of the instruction.

10He said to them, "Go, eat rich food and drink sweet drinks, and send portions to anyone who has nothing prepared, for this day is holy to our Lord. Do not be grieved, for the joy of the LORD is your strength."

11The Levites calmed all the people, saying, "Be quiet, for this day is holy. Do not be grieved."

12All the people went away to eat and drink, to send portions and to celebrate with great joy, because they had understood the words that had been made known to them.

The Festival of Booths

13On the second day the heads of the fathers' houses of all the people, with the priests and the Levites, gathered to Ezra the scribe to study the words of the instruction.

14They found written in the instruction, which the LORD had commanded through Moses, that the sons of Israel should live in booths during the festival in the seventh month,

15and that they should proclaim and spread the word in all their towns and in Jerusalem, saying, "Go out to the hills and bring branches of olive, of wild olive, of myrtle, of palm and of leafy trees, to make booths, as it is written."

16So the people went out and brought them, and made booths for themselves, each on his roof, in their courtyards, in the courts of the house of God, in the square of the Water Gate and in the square of the Gate of Ephraim.

17All the assembly of those who had returned from the captivity made booths and lived in the booths, for from the days of Jeshua son of Nun to that day the sons of Israel had not done so. There was very great joy.

18Day by day, from the first day to the last day, he read from the book of the instruction of God. They kept the festival seven days, and on the eighth day there was a solemn assembly, according to the rule.

Notes

  • v2 "on the first day of the seventh month" — the day of the trumpet blast, a holy assembly (Leviticus 23:24). Ezra had come to Jerusalem to teach statute and rule in Israel (Ezra 7:10); this is the day he does it before all the people.

  • vv2–3 "men and women and all who could listen with understanding" — kol mevin lishmoa. Children old enough to follow are counted with the assembly; the same word, mevinim, is used of the Levites who helped the people to understand (v7).

  • v8 "clearly, and gave the sense" — meforash ve-som sekhel. Meforash is the word the king of Persia used of the letter read plainly before me (Ezra 4:18). It may mean read distinctly, or explained, or put into the Aramaic the people spoke; gave the sense says that the reading came with explanation.

  • v10 "the joy of the LORD is your strength" — chedvat YHWH hi ma'uzzekhem. Chedvah is a rare word: in Hebrew it is found again only in the psalm David gave to Asaph, strength and joy are in His place (1 Chronicles 16:27), and in Aramaic at the dedication of the rebuilt house, kept with joy (Ezra 6:16). Ma'oz is a stronghold, a place to take refuge.

  • v15 "branches of olive, of wild olive, of myrtle, of palm and of leafy trees" — Leviticus names the fruit of splendid trees, branches of palm trees, boughs of leafy trees, and willows of the brook (Leviticus 23:40). The list here is not the same; what is written is the booths themselves.

  • v17 "from the days of Jeshua son of Nun" — Yeshua, the later form of the name Joshua, as the high priest Jeshua bears it. The booths were kept on the return (Ezra 3:4), but not like this, by all the assembly, since Joshua's day.

  • v18 "Day by day… he read from the book" — the law of Moses: at the end of every seven years… at the Festival of Booths… you shall read this instruction before all Israel in their hearing (Deuteronomy 31:10–11).

chapters.title: The Levites' Prayer of Confession
chapters.html:
Nehemiah 9

The Day of Confession

1On the twenty-fourth day of this month the sons of Israel gathered with fasting, in sackcloth and with earth on their heads.

2Those of Israelite descent separated themselves from all foreigners, and they stood and confessed their sins and the iniquities of their fathers.

3They stood up in their places and read from the book of the instruction of the LORD their God for a quarter of the day, and for another quarter they confessed and worshiped the LORD their God.

4On the platform of the Levites stood Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani and Chenani, and they cried out with a loud voice to the LORD their God.

5Then the Levites, Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah and Pethahiah, said, "Stand up and bless the LORD your God from everlasting to everlasting. Blessed be Your glorious name, which is exalted above all blessing and praise.

The Prayer

6You are the LORD, You alone. You made the heavens, the heaven of heavens and all their host, the earth and all that is on it, the seas and all that is in them. You give life to them all, and the host of heaven worships You.

7You are the LORD, the God who chose Abram and brought him out of Ur of the Chaldeans and gave him the name Abraham.

8You found his heart faithful before You and made the covenant with him to give the land of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites and the Girgashites, to give it to his offspring. You have kept Your word, for You are righteous.

9You saw the affliction of our fathers in Egypt and heard their cry at the Red Sea,

10and performed signs and wonders against Pharaoh and all his servants and all the people of his land, for You knew that they acted arrogantly against them. You made a name for Yourself, as it is to this day.

11You divided the sea before them, so that they went through the middle of the sea on dry ground, and You threw their pursuers into the depths, like a stone into mighty waters.

12By a pillar of cloud You led them by day, and by a pillar of fire by night, to light for them the way in which they should go.

13You came down on Mount Sinai and spoke with them from heaven, and gave them right rules and true instructions, good statutes and commandments.

14You made known to them Your holy sabbath, and commanded them commandments and statutes and instruction through Moses Your servant.

15You gave them bread from heaven for their hunger and brought water out of the rock for their thirst, and You told them to go in and possess the land that You had sworn to give them.

16But they, our fathers, acted arrogantly and stiffened their necks and did not obey Your commandments.

17They refused to obey and did not remember the wonders that You had done among them, but stiffened their necks and appointed a leader to return to their slavery in Egypt. But You are a God of forgiveness, gracious and merciful, slow to anger and abundant in loyal love, and You did not forsake them.

18Even when they made for themselves a molten calf and said, 'This is your god who brought you up out of Egypt,' and committed great blasphemies,

19You in Your great mercies did not forsake them in the wilderness. The pillar of cloud did not depart from them by day, to lead them on the way, nor the pillar of fire by night, to light for them the way in which they should go.

20You gave Your good Spirit to instruct them, and did not withhold Your manna from their mouth, and gave them water for their thirst.

21Forty years You sustained them in the wilderness, and they lacked nothing. Their clothes did not wear out, and their feet did not swell.

22You gave them kingdoms and peoples and allotted them to every corner. They took possession of the land of Sihon, the land of the king of Heshbon, and the land of Og king of Bashan.

23You multiplied their sons like the stars of heaven and brought them into the land that You had told their fathers to enter and possess.

24So the sons went in and possessed the land. You subdued before them the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, and gave them into their hand, with their kings and the peoples of the land, to do with them as they would.

25They captured fortified cities and a rich land, and took possession of houses full of all good things, cisterns already hewn, vineyards, olive groves and fruit trees in abundance. They ate and were filled and grew fat, and delighted themselves in Your great goodness.

26But they were disobedient and rebelled against You and cast Your instruction behind their backs. They killed Your prophets, who had warned them in order to turn them back to You, and they committed great blasphemies.

27So You gave them into the hand of their adversaries, who oppressed them. In the time of their distress they cried out to You, and You heard from heaven, and according to Your great mercies You gave them saviors who saved them from the hand of their adversaries.

28But as soon as they had rest, they did evil again before You, and You abandoned them to the hand of their enemies, so that they ruled over them. Yet when they turned and cried out to You, You heard from heaven, and many times You delivered them according to Your mercies.

29You warned them in order to turn them back to Your instruction, yet they acted arrogantly and did not obey Your commandments, but sinned against Your rules, which a person shall do and live by them. They turned a stubborn shoulder and stiffened their neck and would not obey.

30Many years You bore with them and warned them by Your Spirit through Your prophets, yet they would not listen. So You gave them into the hand of the peoples of the lands.

31Yet in Your great mercies You did not make an end of them or forsake them, for You are a gracious and merciful God.

32Now, our God, the great, the mighty and the awesome God, who keeps covenant and loyal love, do not let all the hardship seem little before You that has come on us, on our kings, our officials, our priests, our prophets, our fathers and all Your people, since the days of the kings of Assyria until this day.

33You are righteous in all that has come on us, for You have dealt faithfully and we have acted wickedly.

34Our kings, our officials, our priests and our fathers have not kept Your instruction or paid attention to Your commandments and Your testimonies with which You warned them.

35Even in their own kingdom, in the great goodness You gave them, in the wide and rich land that You set before them, they did not serve You or turn from their evil deeds.

36Here we are, slaves today, slaves in the land that You gave to our fathers to eat its fruit and its good things.

37Its rich yield goes to the kings You have set over us because of our sins. They rule over our bodies and over our livestock as they please, and we are in great distress.

38Because of all this we are making a firm agreement in writing, and on the sealed document are the names of our officials, our Levites and our priests."

Notes

  • vv1–38 — the Hebrew numbers v38 as 10:1. The rendering follows the English numbering.

  • v6 "You are the LORD, You alone" — the Hebrew does not name the one who prays; it follows the Levites' call to bless (v5). The Greek begins And Ezra said.

  • vv7–8 "You found his heart faithful before You" — ne'eman, from the root of Abram believed the LORD (Genesis 15:6). The covenant was made with a man whose heart was found to be trusting.

  • v11 "like a stone into mighty waters" — the song at the sea: they went down into the depths like a stone (Exodus 15:5).

  • v17 "appointed a leader to return to their slavery in Egypt" — the Hebrew has be-miryam, in their rebellion; the Greek has in Egypt, be-Mitsrayim in Hebrew, one letter more. The rendering follows the Greek, because the verse quotes the people in the wilderness: Let us appoint a leader and return to Egypt (Numbers 14:4). A God of forgiveness, gracious and merciful, slow to anger and abundant in loyal love is the name proclaimed on Sinai (Exodus 34:6).

  • v18 "This is your god who brought you up out of Egypt" — Exodus has the plural, These are your gods, Israel (Exodus 32:4). The prayer speaks of the one calf the people made.

  • v21 "Their clothes did not wear out, and their feet did not swell" — the words of Moses: Your clothes did not wear out on you, and your foot did not swell these forty years (Deuteronomy 8:4).

  • v25 "houses full of all good things, cisterns already hewn… grew fat" — the promise of Deuteronomy, houses full of all good things that you did not fill, and hewn cisterns that you did not hew (Deuteronomy 6:11), and its warning, Jeshurun grew fat and kicked (32:15).

  • v29 "which a person shall do and live by them" — the words of the law: the person who does them shall live by them (Leviticus 18:5).

  • vv36–37 "Here we are, slaves today, slaves in the land" — avadim, twice. The land given to the fathers is theirs again, and they work it for the king of Persia.

chapters.title: The Sealed Agreement
chapters.html:
Nehemiah 10

Those Who Set Their Seal

1On the sealed document were: Nehemiah the governor, son of Hacaliah, and Zedekiah;

2Seraiah, Azariah, Jeremiah,

3Pashhur, Amariah, Malchijah,

4Hattush, Shebaniah, Malluch,

5Harim, Meremoth, Obadiah,

6Daniel, Ginnethon, Baruch,

7Meshullam, Abijah, Mijamin,

8Maaziah, Bilgai and Shemaiah. These were the priests.

9The Levites: Jeshua son of Azaniah, Binnui of the sons of Henadad, Kadmiel,

10and their brothers Shebaniah, Hodiah, Kelita, Pelaiah, Hanan,

11Mica, Rehob, Hashabiah,

12Zaccur, Sherebiah, Shebaniah,

13Hodiah, Bani and Beninu.

14The chiefs of the people: Parosh, Pahath-moab, Elam, Zattu, Bani,

15Bunni, Azgad, Bebai,

16Adonijah, Bigvai, Adin,

17Ater, Hezekiah, Azzur,

18Hodiah, Hashum, Bezai,

19Hariph, Anathoth, Nebai,

20Magpiash, Meshullam, Hezir,

21Meshezabel, Zadok, Jaddua,

22Pelatiah, Hanan, Anaiah,

23Hoshea, Hananiah, Hasshub,

24Hallohesh, Pilha, Shobek,

25Rehum, Hashabnah, Maaseiah,

26Ahiah, Hanan, Anan,

27Malluch, Harim and Baanah.

The Terms of the Agreement

28The rest of the people, the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, the temple servants and all who had separated themselves from the peoples of the lands to the instruction of God, their wives, their sons and their daughters, all who had knowledge and understanding,

29join their brothers, their nobles, and enter into a curse and an oath to walk in the instruction of God, which was given through Moses the servant of God, and to keep and do all the commandments of the LORD our Lord and His rules and His statutes:

30We will not give our daughters to the peoples of the land or take their daughters for our sons.

31If the peoples of the land bring goods or any grain to sell on the sabbath day, we will not buy from them on the sabbath or on a holy day. We will let the seventh year lie fallow, and cancel every debt.

32We also lay on ourselves the obligation to give a third of a shekel each year for the service of the house of our God:

33for the bread set in rows, the continual grain offering and the continual burnt offering, the sabbaths, the new moons, the appointed feasts, the holy things and the sin offerings to make atonement for Israel, and for all the work of the house of our God.

34We, the priests, the Levites and the people, have also cast lots for the wood offering, to bring it into the house of our God by our fathers' houses at appointed times year by year, to burn on the altar of the LORD our God, as it is written in the instruction.

35We will bring the firstfruits of our ground and the firstfruits of every fruit of every tree year by year to the house of the LORD,

36and the firstborn of our sons and of our livestock, as it is written in the instruction, and the firstborn of our herds and our flocks, to bring them to the house of our God, to the priests who minister in the house of our God.

37We will bring the first of our dough, our contributions, the fruit of every tree, the new wine and the oil to the priests, to the chambers of the house of our God, and the tithe of our ground to the Levites, for it is the Levites who collect the tithes in all our towns where we work.

38A priest, a son of Aaron, shall be with the Levites when the Levites collect the tithes, and the Levites shall bring up a tenth of the tithes to the house of our God, to the chambers of the storehouse.

  • vv1–39 — the Hebrew numbers these verses 10:2–40; its 10:1 is the English 9:38. The rendering follows the English numbering.

  • v1 "Nehemiah the governor" — the man who tells the story is named first among those who set their seal, in the third person, as a document names its signers.

  • v29 "enter into a curse and an oath" — ba'im be-alah u-vi-shvu'ah, as Moses made the people enter into the covenant of the LORD your God, and into His oath (Deuteronomy 29:12): the people bind themselves to be cursed if they break it.

  • v31 "We will let the seventh year lie fallow, and cancel every debt" — two laws joined: in the seventh year you shall let it rest and lie fallow (Exodus 23:11), ve-nittosh, the same verb; and every creditor shall release what he has lent (Deuteronomy 15:2).

  • v32 "a third of a shekel each year" — the law of the census asked half a shekel of each man (Exodus 30:13), once. The agreement makes a smaller gift a yearly one.

  • v34 "the wood offering… as it is written in the instruction" — what is written is that the fire on the altar shall be kept burning; it shall not go out.   • v38 "a tenth of the tithes" — ma'sar ha-ma'aser, the law of Numbers: the Levites give a tithe of the tithe to the LORD (Numbers 18:26).

  • v39 "We will not neglect the house of our God" — lo na'azov, the last words of the agreement. When Nehemiah comes back, his charge to the officials will be Why is the house of God neglected? (13:11), the same verb.

Nehemiah 11

One in Ten for the Holy City

1The leaders of the people lived in Jerusalem, and the rest of the people cast lots to bring one in ten to live in Jerusalem, the holy city, while nine tenths stayed in the towns.

2The people blessed all the men who willingly offered to live in Jerusalem.

3These are the chiefs of the province who lived in Jerusalem; but in the towns of Judah each lived on his own property in their towns: Israel, the priests, the Levites, the temple servants and the sons of Solomon's servants.

In Jerusalem

4In Jerusalem lived some of the sons of Judah and of the sons of Benjamin. Of the sons of Judah: Athaiah son of Uzziah, son of Zechariah, son of Amariah, son of Shephatiah, son of Mahalalel, of the sons of Perez;

5and Maaseiah son of Baruch, son of Col-hozeh, son of Hazaiah, son of Adaiah, son of Joiarib, son of Zechariah, son of the Shilonite.

6All the sons of Perez who lived in Jerusalem were four hundred and sixty-eight men of valor.

7These are the sons of Benjamin: Sallu son of Meshullam, son of Joed, son of Pedaiah, son of Kolaiah, son of Maaseiah, son of Ithiel, son of Jeshaiah,

8and after him Gabbai and Sallai, nine hundred and twenty-eight.

9Joel son of Zichri was their overseer, and Judah son of Hassenuah was second over the city.

10Of the priests: Jedaiah son of Joiarib, Jachin,

11Seraiah son of Hilkiah, son of Meshullam, son of Zadok, son of Meraioth, son of Ahitub, the chief officer of the house of God,

12and their brothers who did the work of the house, eight hundred and twenty-two; and Adaiah son of Jeroham, son of Pelaliah, son of Amzi, son of Zechariah, son of Pashhur, son of Malchijah,

13and his brothers, heads of fathers' houses, two hundred and forty-two; and Amashsai son of Azarel, son of Ahzai, son of Meshillemoth, son of Immer,

14and their brothers, mighty men of valor, a hundred and twenty-eight. Their overseer was Zabdiel son of Haggedolim.

15Of the Levites: Shemaiah son of Hasshub, son of Azrikam, son of Hashabiah, son of Bunni;

16Shabbethai and Jozabad, of the chiefs of the Levites, who were over the outside work of the house of God;

17Mattaniah son of Mica, son of Zabdi, son of Asaph, the leader who began the thanksgiving in prayer, and Bakbukiah, the second among his brothers; and Abda son of Shammua, son of Galal, son of Jeduthun.

18All the Levites in the holy city were two hundred and eighty-four.

19The gatekeepers: Akkub, Talmon and their brothers, who kept watch at the gates, a hundred and seventy-two.

20The rest of Israel, the priests and the Levites were in all the towns of Judah, each on his own inheritance.

21The temple servants lived on the Ophel, and Ziha and Gishpa were over the temple servants.

22The overseer of the Levites in Jerusalem was Uzzi son of Bani, son of Hashabiah, son of Mattaniah, son of Mica, of the sons of Asaph, the singers, over the work of the house of God.

23For there was a command from the king concerning them, and a fixed provision for the singers, as each day required.

24Pethahiah son of Meshezabel, of the sons of Zerah son of Judah, was at the king's hand in every matter concerning the people.

In the Villages

25As for the villages with their fields, some of the sons of Judah lived in Kiriath-arba and its towns, in Dibon and its towns, in Jekabzeel and its villages,

26in Jeshua, in Moladah, in Beth-pelet,

27in Hazar-shual, in Beersheba and its towns,

28in Ziklag, in Meconah and its towns,

29in En-rimmon, in Zorah, in Jarmuth,

30Zanoah, Adullam and their villages, Lachish and its fields, Azekah and its towns. So they camped from Beersheba to the Valley of Hinnom.

31The sons of Benjamin lived from Geba onward, at Michmash, Aija, Bethel and its towns,

32Anathoth, Nob, Ananiah,

33Hazor, Ramah, Gittaim,

34Hadid, Zeboim, Neballat,

35Lod and Ono, the Valley of Craftsmen.

36Some divisions of the Levites of Judah were joined to Benjamin.

Notes

  • v1 "to bring one in ten to live in Jerusalem, the holy city" — a tenth of the people, given to the city as a tithe is given. Ir ha-qodesh, the holy city, Isaiah's name for it: Put on your beautiful garments, Jerusalem, the holy city (Isaiah 52:1). The wall was finished, but the city was nearly empty (7:4).

  • v2 "all the men who willingly offered" — ha-mitnaddevim, the word of the freewill offering. Some went by lot; some gave themselves.

  • vv3–24 and 1 Chronicles 9:2–34 — Chronicles gives a list of the first inhabitants who lived on their property in their towns in Jerusalem, many of the same names and families, with its own numbers.

  • v9 "second over the city" — al ha-ir mishneh, which may mean second in command of the city or over the Second Quarter of the city, where Huldah lived (2 Kings 22:14).

  • v14 "Zabdiel son of Haggedolim" — ha-gedolim, the great ones. It may be a family name, or say that he came of a leading family.

  • v17 "the leader who began the thanksgiving in prayer" — the line of Asaph, whom David set to give thanks to the LORD (1 Chronicles 16:7), still leads the praise.

  • vv25–30 "Kiriath-arba… from Beersheba to the Valley of Hinnom" — the towns of Judah's old allotment, from Hebron, once Kiriath-arba (Joshua 14:15), to the valley that was Judah's border below Jerusalem (Joshua 15:8). The returned people camped across the land their fathers had held.

chapters.title: The Dedication of the Wall
chapters.html:
Nehemiah 12

Priests and Levites

1These are the priests and the Levites who came up with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and with Jeshua: Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra,

2Amariah, Malluch, Hattush,

3Shecaniah, Rehum, Meremoth,

4Iddo, Ginnethoi, Abijah,

5Mijamin, Maadiah, Bilgah,

6Shemaiah, Joiarib, Jedaiah,

7Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah and Jedaiah. These were the chiefs of the priests and of their brothers in the days of Jeshua.

8The Levites: Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah, who with his brothers was in charge of the songs of thanksgiving.

9Bakbukiah and Unni, their brothers, stood opposite them by watches.

10Jeshua fathered Joiakim, Joiakim fathered Eliashib, Eliashib fathered Joiada,

11Joiada fathered Jonathan, and Jonathan fathered Jaddua.

12In the days of Joiakim the priests, the heads of fathers' houses, were: of Seraiah, Meraiah; of Jeremiah, Hananiah;

13of Ezra, Meshullam; of Amariah, Jehohanan;

14of Melicu, Jonathan; of Shebaniah, Joseph;

15of Harim, Adna; of Meraioth, Helkai;

16of Iddo, Zechariah; of Ginnethon, Meshullam;

17of Abijah, Zichri; of Miniamin; of Moadiah, Piltai;

18of Bilgah, Shammua; of Shemaiah, Jehonathan;

19of Joiarib, Mattenai; of Jedaiah, Uzzi;

20of Sallai, Kallai; of Amok, Eber;

21of Hilkiah, Hashabiah; of Jedaiah, Nethanel.

22In the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan and Jaddua, the Levites were recorded as heads of fathers' houses, and the priests also, until the reign of Darius the Persian.

23The sons of Levi, the heads of fathers' houses, were written in the book of the chronicles until the days of Johanan son of Eliashib.

24The chiefs of the Levites were Hashabiah, Sherebiah and Jeshua son of Kadmiel, with their brothers opposite them, to praise and to give thanks according to the command of David the man of God, watch answering watch.

25Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon and Akkub were gatekeepers keeping watch at the storehouses of the gates.

26These served in the days of Joiakim son of Jeshua, son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor and of Ezra the priest, the scribe.

The Dedication

27At the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem they sought out the Levites from all their places to bring them to Jerusalem, to celebrate the dedication with joy, with thanksgivings and with singing, with cymbals, harps and lyres.

28The sons of the singers gathered together from the district around Jerusalem and from the villages of the Netophathites,

29from Beth-gilgal and from the fields of Geba and Azmaveth, for the singers had built villages for themselves around Jerusalem.

30The priests and the Levites purified themselves, and they purified the people, the gates and the wall.

31Then I brought the leaders of Judah up onto the wall and appointed two great choirs of thanksgiving. One went to the right on the wall, toward the Dung Gate.

32After them went Hoshaiah and half of the leaders of Judah,

33and Azariah, Ezra, Meshullam,

34Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah and Jeremiah,

35and some of the sons of the priests with trumpets: Zechariah son of Jonathan, son of Shemaiah, son of Mattaniah, son of Micaiah, son of Zaccur, son of Asaph,

36and his brothers Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah and Hanani, with the instruments of song of David the man of God. Ezra the scribe went before them.

37At the Fountain Gate they went straight up the steps of the City of David, at the ascent of the wall above the house of David, to the Water Gate on the east.

38The second choir of thanksgiving went the opposite way, and I followed it with half of the people, on the wall, above the Tower of the Ovens, to the Broad Wall,

39and above the Gate of Ephraim, by the Old Gate, by the Fish Gate, the Tower of Hananel and the Tower of the Hundred, to the Sheep Gate. They stopped at the Gate of the Guard.

40So both choirs of thanksgiving stood in the house of God, and I and half of the officials with me,

41and the priests Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah and Hananiah, with trumpets,

42and Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam and Ezer. The singers sang, with Jezrahiah as their leader.

43They offered great sacrifices that day and rejoiced, for God had made them rejoice with great joy. The women and the children also rejoiced, and the joy of Jerusalem was heard far away.

Portions for the Priests and Levites

44On that day men were appointed over the chambers for the stores, the contributions, the firstfruits and the tithes, to gather into them from the fields of the towns the portions required by the instruction for the priests and for the Levites, for Judah rejoiced over the priests and the Levites who served.

45They kept the charge of their God and the charge of purification, as did the singers and the gatekeepers, according to the command of David and of Solomon his son.

46For long ago, in the days of David and Asaph, there were chiefs of the singers, and songs of praise and thanksgiving to God.

47In the days of Zerubbabel and in the days of Nehemiah all Israel gave the portions for the singers and the gatekeepers, as each day required. They set apart what was holy for the Levites, and the Levites set apart what was holy for the sons of Aaron.

Notes

  • vv10–11, 22 "Jeshua fathered Joiakim… Jonathan fathered Jaddua… until the reign of Darius the Persian" — the high priests' line runs past Nehemiah's own day, five generations from Jeshua of the first return. Which Darius is meant the verse does not say.

  • v23 "the book of the chronicles" — sefer divrei ha-yamim, the book of the matters of the days, the Hebrew title of the book of Chronicles. Whether that book is meant, or a temple register, the verse does not say.

  • v24 "watch answering watch" — mishmar le-ummat mishmar, the two halves of the singers set opposite each other to answer in turn, according to the command of David.

  • vv27, 43 "the dedication… with joy" — chanukkah, the word of the dedication of the altar (Numbers 7:10) and of the house (Ezra 6:16). Joy, simchah, and its verb come five times in v43.

  • vv31–40 "two great choirs of thanksgiving" — one goes right, one goes left, around the wall that had been rebuilt, and they meet in the house of God. The right-hand choir passes the Dung Gate and the Fountain Gate, where Nehemiah rode by night to see the ruins (2:13–14).

  • v36 "Ezra the scribe went before them" — Ezra leads one choir, and Nehemiah follows the other (v38). The book shows the two men together in one scene only here and at the reading of the instruction (8:9).

  • v43 "the joy of Jerusalem was heard far away" — me-rachoq, as at the laying of the foundation, when the sound was heard far away and no one could tell the shout of joy from the weeping (Ezra 3:13). Here there is only joy.

On that day men were appointed over the chambers for the stores, the contributions, the firstfruits and the tithes, to gather into them from the fields of the towns the portions required by the instruction for the priests and for the Levites, for Judah rejoiced over the priests and the Levites who served.
They kept the charge of their God and the charge of purification, as did the singers and the gatekeepers, according to the command of David and of Solomon his son.
For long ago, in the days of David and Asaph, there were chiefs of the singers, and songs of praise and thanksgiving to God.

In the days of Zerubbabel and in the days of Nehemiah all Israel gave the portions for the singers and the gatekeepers, as each day required. They set apart what was holy for the Levites, and the Levites set apart what was holy for the sons of Aaron.

chapters.title: Nehemiah's Last Reforms
chapters.html:
Nehemiah 13

Separation from the Foreigners

1On that day they read from the book of Moses in the hearing of the people, and it was found written in it that no Ammonite or Moabite should ever enter the assembly of God,

2because they did not meet the sons of Israel with bread and water, but hired Balaam against them to curse them. Yet our God turned the curse into a blessing.

3When they heard the instruction, they separated from Israel all who were of mixed descent.

Tobiah Thrown Out

4Before this, Eliashib the priest, who was appointed over the chambers of the house of our God and was related to Tobiah,

5had prepared for him a large chamber where they had formerly put the grain offering, the frankincense, the vessels, and the tithes of grain, new wine and oil, which were commanded for the Levites, the singers and the gatekeepers, and the contributions for the priests.

6While all this was going on, I was not in Jerusalem, for in the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon I went to the king. After some time I asked leave of the king

7and came to Jerusalem, and I learned of the evil Eliashib had done for Tobiah, preparing a chamber for him in the courts of the house of God.

8It displeased me greatly, and I threw all of Tobiah's household furniture out of the chamber.

9Then I gave orders, and they purified the chambers, and I brought back there the vessels of the house of God, with the grain offering and the frankincense.

The Levites' Portions

10I also learned that the portions of the Levites had not been given to them, so that the Levites and the singers who did the work had fled, each to his field.

11So I brought charges against the officials and said, "Why is the house of God neglected?" I gathered them together and set them at their posts.

12Then all Judah brought the tithe of the grain, the new wine and the oil into the storehouses.

13I put in charge of the storehouses Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe and Pedaiah of the Levites, and with them Hanan son of Zaccur, son of Mattaniah, for they were counted faithful, and their duty was to distribute to their brothers.

14Remember me, my God, for this, and do not wipe out the loyal deeds that I have done for the house of my God and for its service.

The Sabbath Kept

15In those days I saw in Judah people treading winepresses on the sabbath, bringing in heaps of grain and loading them on donkeys, and also wine, grapes, figs and every kind of load, which they brought into Jerusalem on the sabbath day. I warned them on the day they sold food.

16Men of Tyre who lived in the city brought in fish and every kind of merchandise and sold it on the sabbath to the people of Judah, and in Jerusalem.

17Then I brought charges against the nobles of Judah and said to them, "What is this evil thing you are doing, profaning the sabbath day?

18Did not your fathers act in this way, and did not our God bring all this evil on us and on this city? Yet you are bringing more wrath on Israel by profaning the sabbath."

19When the gates of Jerusalem began to grow dark before the sabbath, I commanded that the doors be shut, and I ordered that they not be opened until after the sabbath. I stationed some of my servants at the gates, so that no load would be brought in on the sabbath day.

20Once or twice the merchants and sellers of every kind of goods spent the night outside Jerusalem.

21But I warned them and said to them, "Why are you spending the night in front of the wall? If you do it again, I will lay hands on you." From that time on they did not come on the sabbath.

22Then I told the Levites to purify themselves and come and guard the gates, to keep the sabbath day holy. Remember me, my God, for this also, and spare me according to the greatness of Your loyal love.

The Foreign Wives

23In those days also I saw Jews who had married women of Ashdod, Ammon and Moab.

24Half of their children spoke the language of Ashdod, or the language of one people or another, and could not speak the language of Judah.

25I brought charges against them and cursed them, beat some of their men and pulled out their hair, and made them swear by God, "You shall not give your daughters to their sons, or take their daughters for your sons or for yourselves.

26Did not Solomon king of Israel sin on account of such women? Among the many nations there was no king like him, and he was loved by his God, and God made him king over all Israel. Yet even him the foreign women made to sin.

27Shall we then listen to you and do all this great evil, breaking faith with our God by marrying foreign women?"

28One of the sons of Joiada, son of Eliashib the high priest, was the son-in-law of Sanballat the Horonite, so I drove him away from me.

29Remember them, my God, because they have defiled the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood and of the Levites.

30So I cleansed them from everything foreign, and I established the duties of the priests and the Levites, each in his work,

31and provided for the wood offering at appointed times, and for the firstfruits. Remember me, my God, for good.

Notes

  • vv1–2 "no Ammonite or Moabite should ever enter the assembly of God… our God turned the curse into a blessing" — the law of Deuteronomy 23:3–5: the LORD your God turned the curse into a blessing for you, because the LORD your God loved you.

  • vv4–9 "a large chamber… I threw all of Tobiah's household furniture out" — the store of the offerings had become the lodging of Tobiah the Ammonite (2:10), whom the law just read shuts out of the assembly.

  • vv10–11 "Why is the house of God neglected?" — ne'ezav, the verb of the people's own pledge, We will not neglect the house of our God (10:39). The agreement broke at its last line first.

  • vv14, 22, 31 "Remember me, my God" — Nehemiah's short prayer, as at 5:19, here three times in one chapter, and the last words of the book. In v14 he asks God not to wipe out his loyal deeds, chasadai; in v22 he asks to be spared according to the greatness of Your loyal love, chasdekha. In v29 the same words are turned against the priests: Remember them, my God.

  • vv15–22 "bringing… into Jerusalem on the sabbath day" — the word of Jeremiah: Do not carry a load on the sabbath day or bring it in by the gates of Jerusalem… if you do not listen… I will kindle a fire in its gates (Jeremiah 17:21, 27). Did not your fathers act in this way? (v18).

  • v24 "could not speak the language of Judah" — Yehudit, the language the king's men begged the Assyrian not to use on the wall (2 Kings 18:26). The children of the city cannot speak it.

  • v25 "beat some of their men and pulled out their hair" — when Ezra heard of the marriages, he pulled out his own hair (Ezra 9:3). Nehemiah pulls out theirs.

  • v26 "he was loved by his God… Yet even him the foreign women made to sin" — Solomon's other name was Jedidiah, beloved of the LORD (2 Samuel 12:25), and his wives turned his heart away after other gods (1 Kings 11:4).
